title: Installing and setting up a Linux distribution

videos.script: The office's shared files live on a small computer in a cupboard. It runs Linux, and it was installed years ago by somebody who has since left. {{cupboard}} It is due for a new installation, and Ana is going to do it herself. {{new}} Installing Linux follows the same shape as installing Windows. Download, make a USB stick, start from it, choose a disk, create a user, update. What differs are the details, and a few of them have no Windows equivalent at all. {{shape}} You choose a distribution, and a version with years of updates ahead of it. You check that the download is exactly what the publisher made, before trusting it with the office's files. {{check}} You can try the system from the stick before installing anything. And you can install it beside Windows on the same disk, if you know the three things Windows needs done first. {{beside}} Once it is installed, you will run its first updates and see how its administrator account works. And you will learn where everything lives in a system that has no drive letters at all. {{after}} The commands in this lesson were run on a freshly installed Ubuntu 24.04, so what you see is what you will get. {{title}}
